SMTO-POL-0007 — SMTO needs your clear go-ahead before pushing past a blocked job

GUID: ade0da11-30a1-42fc-8854-b80a055acd69
Slug: resource-unsafe-confirmation-required
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • SMTO can't tell whether an earlier job is still using what your task needs. Going ahead could let both change the same thing at once, so SMTO won't continue without a matching confirmation. Nothing has run yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and find the task's recovery card in the conversation. A go-ahead must match the exact situation shown on the current card; a missing or old one is refused.
  2. Select Wait until the job state changes on the task's recovery card if the earlier job might still be working. SMTO continues by itself once that job is done. Waiting lets the earlier job finish first, so the two never change the same thing at once.
  3. Select Resolve forcefully by terminating job only if you are sure the earlier job is no longer needed. The button is greyed out when SMTO can't stop it safely. Stopping the earlier job frees what your task needs without two jobs working on it together.

What success looks like

  • The recovery card shows 'Job state updated.' or 'Blocking job claims restored.', and the task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't force the task through while you're unsure whether the earlier job is still running; both could change the same files or device at once.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The resource-reconciliation route refused an override because no override challenge was issued for this recovery candidate, or the submitted challenge ID does not match the one issued.

What this means

  • The unsafe resource-recovery path lacks a matching accepted challenge while prior-operation liveness remains uncertain. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The unsafe resource-recovery path lacks a matching accepted challenge while prior-operation liveness remains uncertain.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original operation's liveness and the current challenge; restored connectivity alone does not prove the old operation stopped.

How to fix it

  • Check the run's resource_reconciliation_request and the candidate's override_challenge (route_groups/resource_reconciliation.py). Send request_override first, then override with that challenge_id against the same blocker_revision, or use the wait/reset actions the projection enables; unsafe override also requires the unsafe-action policy to be 'ask'.
  • Review the exact current recovery action and confirm through the supported flow if intended.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The current recovery challenge is deliberately accepted or declined against unchanged blocker evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
